newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS - Electrolux shares soar on downsize decision.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Electrolux shares soar on downsize decision.

text.p: Shares in Electrolux, the world's largest supplier of household appliances, soared to unprecedented levels on Friday after a sharp job cuts programme was announced a day earlier.
New Chief Executive Michael Treschow stamped his mark on the company with the surprise announcement of a two-year restructuring programme after just two months at the helm.
Treschow said Electrolux would close about 25 of 150 plants and cut 12,000 staff from a workforce of 105,000 in a 2.5 billion crown programme which will be charged against second quarter earnings.

Electrolux's share price had soared 64 crowns by Thursday's close to an all-time high of 529 crowns as markets cheered the willingness of Treschow to tackle the white goods maker's complex structure and address sagging world markets.
Traders thinking Electrolux would run out of steam were taken aback on Friday when the bull run resumed, taking the share another 71 crowns to 600 shortly after the Stockholm bourse opened.
By 1100 GMT the share had eased to 592 crowns but several traders said Electrolux, long held back by concern over its performance in a highly competitive global market, could go even higher.
U.S. investment bank Lehman Brothers analyst Chris Heminway told Reuters he was looking at a mid-term price for Electrolux of 630 crowns.

Lehman said it had added Electrolux to its European strategy "recommended" list as its rating was raised to "outperform" from "underperform," due to its recent restructuring plan, including an 11 percent cut in staff worldwide.

The turnaround in Electrolux's share price fortunes came on the same day that its main competitor, Whirlpool issued a warning that European white good sales were expected to decline again this year for the fifth year running.
Whirlpool predicted a one percent decline in white goods sales in Europe. "The environment (in Europe) is terribly negative," Whirlpool's European head Jeff Fettig told The Financial Times.

Treschow told Reuters Financial Television in an interview that there were signs of a turnaround in the crucial U.S. market, where competition for its Frigidaire unit against Whirlpool is at its toughest.
"We have been losing money for some years on white goods (in the U.S.) but there are some encouraging signs. I'm rather optimistic that we are getting past the time of losing money there," he said.
Treschow said European markets were mixed, strong in Scandinavia and eastern Europe but "very weak" in Germany and soft in France, Italy and Spain.
Market analysts were surprised by the demand for Electrolux stock.

"We are astonished about the performance of the share since they announced their 2.5 billion crown two-year restructuring programme. Many people are disappointed that they did not predict this," one broker said.
"A new managing director has to mark his territory," the broker added.

Some analysts said the job cuts and plant closure programme marked a more aggressive approach by Electrolux, almost a shot across Whirlpool's bows that it is returning to the battle for market share after pursuing the lower end of the household appliance market under former head Leif Johansson.
"Whirlpool has been winning market share and Electrolux has been relaxed about that because they are taking it on the low end of the market," said one analyst.
Some analysts said the announcement was a slap in the face for Johansson and a poor reflection of his performance.
"It's an enormous black mark for the management, that you can quite simply get rid of 12,000 employees. It should have been done a long time ago," one analyst said.
Electrolux said the restructuring costs levied in the second quarter would be partly offset by a capital gain of 600 million crowns from the sale of Husqvarna Sewing Machines.

Electrolux said in a statement that the restructure was designed to boost profit margins. Electrolux has set a long-term financial target to reach an operating margin of 6.5-7.0 percent by the year 2000.
In 1996, Electrolux posted a 19 percent drop in profit after financial items of 3.25 billion crowns, blaming weak European markets.
